Intersection curves of two implicit surfaces

Source: R/layers-stats-volumes.R
stat_isocurve_3d.Rd

Traces the curve where fun1 = levels[1] and fun2 = levels[2] meet, inside the box of the position scales. Both functions are evaluated on an n grid and each cell is split into the six tetrahedra of stat_isosurface_3d(method = "tetra"), on which both are replaced by their linear interpolants. In each tetrahedron the level set of fun1 is a triangle or a quad on which fun2 is linear, so the curve crosses it in one segment; segments end on the faces shared with the neighbouring tetrahedra and are chained into open curves (ending on the box) and closed loops. Each point is then moved onto both level sets by refine Newton steps with the minimum-norm update for the two equations, using central differences of the functions, or exact gradients for signed distance functions (sdf_sphere()). Points where the two surfaces touch tangentially keep their position.

Usage

stat_isocurve_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = ggplot2::GeomPath,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  fun1,
  fun2,
  n = 32L,
  args = list(),
  levels = c(0, 0),
  refine = 2L,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

geom_isocurve_3d(...)

Arguments

mapping, data, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

geom

Geom prototype for keyed triangle corners.

fun1, fun2

Vectorised scalar functions of x, y and z, or signed distance functions.

n

Grid resolution, scalar or three integers.

args

Additional named arguments passed to fun.

levels

The levels of fun1 and fun2.

refine

Number of Newton steps per curve point; 0 keeps the intersection of the linear interpolants.

Details

A curve that lies within a single grid cell, or two curves that pass through one cell, can be missed or joined; a finer n resolves them. Snyder's interval method subdivides until each box holds one curve piece that is monotone in some coordinate.

References

Snyder (1992). Interval analysis for computer graphics. SIGGRAPH '92, 121-130. doi:10.1145/133994.134024

Examples

ggplot2::ggplot() +
  geom_isocurve_3d(fun1 = sdf_sphere(radius = 1),
                   fun2 = function(x, y, z) x^2 - y^2 - z * 0.5, n = 16) +
  ggplot2::xlim(-1.2, 1.2) + ggplot2::ylim(-1.2, 1.2) +
  scale_z_continuous(limits = c(-1.2, 1.2)) + coord_3d()
